title: What happens when you tap to pay

lines.text: One coffee. *Six* stops. *Two* seconds. And *zero* money moved.
Stop one, your phone. | *Face ID* unlocks a separate chip, | a *vault* the rest of the phone can't read.
Stop two, inside the vault. | Not your card number, | but a *stand-in* that only works on this phone. | It signs this one purchase, | so a copy is already *dead.*
Stop three, the reader. | *NFC* only reaches about *four centimeters,* | that's why you have to touch it.
Stop four, the shop's bank. | It reads the first few digits, | sees *Visa,* | and passes it on.
Stop five, Visa. | It swaps the stand-in for your *real* number, | and an AI checks over *500* signals | in about one *millisecond.*
Stop six, your bank. | It checks the *fraud score* and your balance, | and says *yes.* | Beep. Coffee's yours.
But no money moved. | That beep was a *promise.* | The real money moves later, | in a batch called *settlement.*
Want to build stuff like this, | *one lesson* a day? | Head to *Teyro.*

sources: Apple: Apple Pay security and privacy overview (support.apple.com/101554): card numbers not stored on device or Apple servers; Device Account Number stored in the Secure Element, isolated from the OS; after Face ID/Touch ID/passcode the Secure Element provides the Device Account Number + a transaction-specific dynamic security code; neither Apple nor the device sends the actual card number

EMV contactless: the cryptogram covers the transaction data incl. amount and an application transaction counter, so a replay fails (EMVCo Book C / general EMV); contactless operating range up to ~4 cm (EMVCo contactless specification)
Routing: the acquirer routes by the leading digits (BIN/IIN) to the card network
Visa press release 2019 (investor.visa.com): Visa Advanced Authorization evaluates 500+ risk attributes in about one millisecond; risk score 1-99 shared with the issuer
Visa Token Service: the network maps the token back to the card number (de-tokenization) before the issuer authorizes
Settlement: authorization moves no funds; clearing and settlement happen later in batches (typically daily)
Cut from the founder's script: '80,000 messages a second' (Visa 10-K: 'more than 65,000'); 258 billion transactions (true, 257.5B FY2025, cut for length)
